back: The stages followed to produce a program: analysis, design, coding and testing (repeated when problems are found).
Identify the problem and the requirements; use abstraction and decomposition.
Plan the solution: decomposition, structure diagrams, flowcharts, pseudocode, data and interface design.
Coding: write the program with iterative testing of each module. Testing: run the whole program with normal, abnormal, extreme and boundary data.
Removing unnecessary detail so only the information needed to solve the problem remains.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller sub-problems that can each be solved separately.
The four parts of a decomposed problem: data in, what is done to it, information out, data kept for later.
Shows a system broken into sub-systems level by level; each bottom-level box becomes a module.
Top-down: split the whole problem into smaller parts. Bottom-up: build small modules first and combine them into the whole.
notes: ZIMSEC asks for a top-down approach.
